concerns.text: FR-003 requires executing '27 distinct MLLMs' but no model list or selection criterion is pinned anywhere in the spec. An implementer cannot know they are done (which 27? which variants/quantizations?). The assumption only gives one example ('LLaVA-1.5-7B or similar'). Specify the ensemble list or a deterministic selection rule (e.g., 'the 27 models evaluated in arXiv:2605.22109, Table N').

concerns.location: spec.md:US-1 Acceptance Scenario 1 / Assumption about grounding validity
concerns.text: The 'grounding score' and the classification of 'valid grounding' are never defined operationally. US-1 demands 'a grounding score that matches the definition of Prejudice/Holistic-Grounding' but the spec gives no procedure for scoring a reasoning string against metadata (automated string/keyword match? LLM-as-judge? human coding?). Without a stated evaluation procedure, PR/HR are not reproducibly computable and FR-003/SC-001 cannot be confirmed met-or-not.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-2 Acceptance Scenario 1 / Constitution Principle VI
concerns.text: 'the model's output reasoning explicitly cites or incorporates this context' is not verifiable as written — 'incorporates' has no check procedure. Constitution VI demands metrics verify the justification cites the injected norms; specify the check (e.g., named-entity/string overlap with the injected profile, or a documented judge procedure) so Integration-failure Rate is computable.

SC-005 sweeps the grounding threshold 'over a range of absolute differences' but names neither the range nor the sweep points. Per the deferred-values convention the empirical values may be deferred, but the criterion must at least name the sweep parameter and its planned range/reference so robustness is checkable.

The 'grounding uncertainty' flag has no detection criterion — how is a sample identified as having ambiguous or conflicting behavioral evidence in the metadata? Specify the rule (e.g., metadata fields disagree per a named check) so the exclusion from PR is reproducible.
